title: Dusk bot vs Grok Bot for a month of everyday use
h1: dusk bot vs grok bot for a month of use
description: Compare a light month and a heavy month on dusk bot and Grok Bot, then see where your chats live, how phone access works and what happens if you leave.
answer: **if you already pay for ai and mostly work at your desk, dusk bot adds no personal desktop fee.** if you already have x premium, grok bot includes a cloud computer in that bill. the difference shows up when you hit a limit, switch phones or want your files back.[^1][^2][^3][^4]
og_line: price a month, then plan the exit.

them: **you already use the x bundle.** try its included computer before you buy hosting elsewhere.[^1][^5]
**you rely on a native android app.** grok bot has one and can finish cloud work after your phone goes away.[^2]
dusk: **you want your notes on your own disk.** choose the desktop and decide which ai handles each bot.[^6][^7]
**you want different models for different jobs.** changing one bot's model leaves its files and memory in place.[^7]

compare.intro: **follow a chat from the device in your hand to the machine that keeps it.** these choices affect what you can still reach at the end of the month.

rows.label: time to get started
cells: desktop setup starts with your ai sign-in. optional dusk cloud takes about a minute
download the app and sign in with cursor. the faq gives no time estimate

rows.label: where your data lives
cells: chats and files live on your desktop, your server or your dusk cloud machine
cloud storage required. bots share files, browser sessions and logins on your cloud computer

rows.label: who sees the prompt
cells: from the bot’s machine straight to the ai provider you chose
cursor’s privacy settings apply. a provider on its sub-processor list may handle the task

rows.label: if you change your mind about the ai
cells: switch a single bot to another model and keep its chat
no model picker, visible model name or personal api key

rows.label: what works on your phone
cells: iphone app. android uses a paired browser until the store app arrives. that browser has no notifications
iphone, ipad and android apps. no general web chat

rows.label: if you stop paying
cells: local bots carry on. dusk holds a canceled cloud machine for 30 days before deletion
access depends on a qualifying plan. account deletion is a separate decision that also deletes cursor

rows.label: what you can save first
cells: password-protected full backup, excluding sign-ins and keys
download individual files or all files. a bot template leaves out conversations and memory

sections.h: a light month at your own desk
sections.md:
**compare the extra cost against what you already pay.** suppose you use a bot occasionally for personal work. your current ai plan covers it, and your computer is awake when you need it. for grok, assume monthly premium and usage within the weekly pool.[^1][^4][^12]

```text
dusk desktop: existing ai bill + $0 = existing ai bill
grok, new subscriber: $30 premium + $0 overage = $30
grok, already on premium: $30 total - $30 already budgeted = $0 extra
```

if you plan to keep premium for cursor anyway, switching the bot alone won't save that $30.

sections.h: a heavy month with the laptop shut
sections.md:
**price the computer and the extra ai separately.** suppose you want a hosted machine for work. dusk pro includes a work license. on grok, compare a monthly tier such as ultra. neither price tells you how much your particular job will use.[^1][^3][^4][^12]

```text
dusk pro: $12 work license + $38 hosting = $50
month on dusk pro = $50 + your provider's ai charges
month on x ultra = $200 + prepaid credits used beyond the pool
```

ultra is an example, not a requirement for heavy use. grok publishes relative allowances but no fixed number of finished tasks. on dusk, a larger cloud machine does not buy more ai from your provider. use your own bill to fill in the missing amount.[^3][^4][^12]

sections.h: the last day of the subscription
sections.md:
**save anything you need before you give up access.** a dusk backup leaves out credentials. restoring it replaces the current setup and brings routines back paused.[^6]

on grok, downloading files and sharing a bot template serve different purposes. neither gives you a full chat archive.[^11] deleting the cursor account removes bots, chats and computers, with a purge within 30 days.[^2] use the [migration steps](/guides/move-from-grok-bot) if you want to keep the bot’s working setup.

method: **these examples show bills, not a speed test.** we make dusk bot. the grok plan and app details come from sources checked on 20 november 2026. for each example we state what the person already pays for. neither company quotes a per-task price for the work in those examples.

faq.q: do i need a dusk subscription to use it on my phone?
faq.a: **you can pair your phone to the desktop for personal use.** leave the computer on and dusk running. pair to dusk cloud instead if you need replies when the computer is off.[^4][^10]

faq.q: is grok bot free if i have a cursor subscription?
faq.a: **eligible legacy cursor plans already include it.** paid individual plans and self-serve teams qualify. usage beyond the weekly pool can still reach on-demand billing. see the [pricing breakdown](/guides/grok-bot-pricing).[^2][^12]
